reason: This is the only offered action, and collisions should help organize the orbiting debris.
expectation: I expect the debris to change through collisions, perhaps concentrating or spreading into a disk; the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The collisions redistributed the debris into a spreading ring, which can now follow either an outward or inward path.
reaction: The distinction between a spreading disk and a solid ring is useful.
reason: I want to follow the material beyond the tidal disruption region toward forming the Moon.
expectation: I expect some rock to reach a region where it can gather without being torn apart, though the immediate result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Gravity may return debris to Earth, but I want to follow Moon formation first.

effect: Beyond the disruptive tidal region, debris has formed moonlets that can survive and merge.
reaction: It is satisfying to see why distance from Earth matters for clumping.
reason: Gravity within the swarm should help the moonlets gather into a larger body.
expectation: I expect the moonlets to merge into a larger Moon-forming body, though its immediate state is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth is another goal, but I want to continue forming the Moon first.

effect: The moonlets have gathered into a hot young Moon, which still needs to cool.
reaction: The progression from debris to a substantial satellite is satisfying.
reason: Open space should let the hot Moon lose heat and advance the cooling-crust goal.
expectation: I expect the Moon to cool, perhaps forming a crust, though the immediate result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth remains a goal, but I want to finish the Moon’s cooling path first.

effect: Cooling has formed lunar magma-ocean crystals, suggesting they can contribute to a crust.
reaction: The distinction between sinking and floating minerals is interesting.
reason: Combine the crystals with the young Moon to continue forming its crust.
expectation: I expect some crystals to form a lunar crust, though the immediate result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth remains necessary, but I want to finish the Moon's cooling path first.

effect: Buoyant plagioclase has formed a floating layer within the Moon, which can now cool further into crust.
reaction: The density-based separation makes the crust formation clearer.
reason: Continue cooling the floating layer to advance the lunar crust goal.
expectation: I expect the floating layer to cool into a more solid lunar crust.

alternatives.reason: Returning debris to Earth is still necessary, but I want to finish the crust first.

effect: The Moon now has a pale early crust, completing that goal; returning debris to Earth remains.
reaction: The cooling sequence made the crust's origin clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action and should advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect Earth's gravity to draw some of the spreading debris inward, though the immediate result is uncertain.

effect: The inward-moving debris is falling back toward Earth rather than joining the Moon.
reaction: The two different fates of the debris are clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action and should return the falling rock to Earth.
expectation: I expect the debris to rejoin Earth, completing the remaining goal.

effect: The falling debris rejoined and heated Earth, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast between debris forming the Moon and debris returning to Earth gave the ending a clear purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the lunar crystals into a floating feldspar-rich layer was most worthwhile: buoyancy made the origin of the early crust understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final return of debris was clear but predictable, with only one gameplay action offered at each of the last two decisions.

surprise.text: I was interested that relatively buoyant plagioclase could float and help build the Moon's pale crust.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining the crystals with the young Moon was less physically explicit than the resulting explanation of flotation.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the remade Earth cools and how water reaches the surface; the chapter connected its steps to understandable physical processes.
